nodes.title: The exceptional primes of E
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve of conductor N and j-invariant j_E. Its exceptional set Σ_E is the finite set of primes p such that p ≤ 5, or p ∣ N, or p ∣ v_ℓ(j_E) for some prime ℓ with v_ℓ(N) = 1, or E admits a ℚ-rational cyclic subgroup of order p (a subgroup of E(ℚ̄) of order p stable under Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ); equivalently the kernel of a ℚ-rational isogeny of degree p). Here p ∣ N means bad reduction at p and v_ℓ(N) = 1 means multiplicative reduction at ℓ, so Σ_E is defined through reduction types and does not need the conductor exponents. Every p ∉ Σ_E is good for E and E[p] is irreducible.
hypotheses: Σ_E depends only on the ℚ-isomorphism class of E; it is finite by the finiteness of the prime degrees of rational isogenies (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.6) and because only finitely many ℓ have v_ℓ(N) = 1, each with v_ℓ(j_E) a fixed negative integer.
proofSteps: Rational cyclic p-subgroups C give ℚ-isogenies E → E/C of degree p; there are finitely many E/C up to ℚ-isomorphism (finiteness of the isogeny class), and for each E′ the nonzero Hom_ℚ(E, E′) = ℤ·f₀ has degrees d·n², so only finitely many primes p occur as degrees (R28.6: End_ℚ(E) = ℤ, rank-one Hom).
The multiplicative-reduction condition is finite: finitely many ℓ ∥ N, each with v_ℓ(j_E) ≠ 0.
Assemble the four finite sets.
acceptance: Keep Σ_E as data: every later step says which of its clauses it uses.
Do not assume Serre's open-image theorem or exclude CM curves: the finiteness argument uses only R28.6.
Mazur's bound (p > 163 for irreducibility) is a sharper, unread input; it is not needed for finiteness.

The unit tests separate the clauses at the prime 7. 26b1 triggers the rational-isogeny clause and the valuation clause together; 274a1 triggers only the valuation clause; 162b1 triggers only the rational-isogeny clause; 11a1 triggers neither. A definition that drops either clause, or that adds primes, fails one of them.

nodes.title: The residual conductor divides N
nodes.statement: For every prime p, the prime-to-p Artin conductor N(ρ̄_{E,p}) of E[p] divides N; at each ℓ ≠ p the exponent of ℓ in N(ρ̄_{E,p}) is at most v_ℓ(N).
hypotheses: Conductors: the Artin conductor of the residual representation away from p and the conductor of E through its ℓ-adic Tate modules (R01.6's conductor interface).
proofSteps: Fix ℓ ≠ p and compare E[p] with T_p(E) (p ≠ ℓ); the conductor exponent of V_r(E) at ℓ does not depend on r ≠ ℓ (R01.6).
Tame part: E[p]^{I_ℓ} contains the reduction of T_p(E)^{I_ℓ}, a saturated sublattice, so dim E[p] − dim E[p]^{I_ℓ} ≤ 2 − dim V_p(E)^{I_ℓ}.
Wild part: wild inertia is pro-ℓ and acts on T_p(E) through a finite ℓ-group, of order prime to p, so reduction mod p preserves its character and the Swan conductors of E[p] and V_p(E) agree.
acceptance: Serre notes that divisibility alone suffices for Theoreme 4.

nodes.title: When the residual conductor equals N
nodes.statement: For p ≥ 5: N(ρ̄_{E,p}) = N iff (a) p ∤ N and (b) p ∤ v_ℓ(j_E) for every ℓ with v_ℓ(N) = 1. In particular N(ρ̄_{E,p}) = N for every p ∉ Σ_E.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 is what makes the additive places harmless: the image of inertia at an additive place of potentially good reduction has order dividing 24.
Serre states the criterion for p > 5 ('on vérifie', no proof); the argument below also covers p = 5, since it needs only p odd and p ∤ 24. Only p ∉ Σ_E (so p ≥ 7) is used in R29.2–R29.6.
proofSteps: If p ∣ N then p divides N but not the prime-to-p conductor: (a) is necessary.
At ℓ ∥ N (multiplicative reduction) E is, up to an unramified quadratic twist, the Tate curve with parameter q, v_ℓ(q) = −v_ℓ(j_E); E[p] is unramified at ℓ iff p ∣ v_ℓ(q). This is condition (b).

At additive ℓ, V_r(E)^{I_ℓ} = 0 and the inertia image is finite of order dividing 24 (potentially good) or acts through a nontrivial quadratic character times a unipotent (potentially multiplicative); for p ≥ 5 the reduction E[p]^{I_ℓ} is also 0 and the Swan conductors agree, so the exponents are equal.
acceptance: Test: a semistable E with ℓ ∥ N, p ∣ v_ℓ(j_E) and p ∤ v_{ℓ′}(j_E) for every other ℓ′ ∣ N has N(ρ̄_{E,p}) = N/ℓ (the level-lowering situation).
Serre gives the criterion with 'on vérifie' and no proof; the argument here follows the Tate curve at ℓ.

A Galois-stable line in E[p] is a ℚ-rational cyclic subgroup of order p, excluded for p ∉ Σ_E.
Odd p with det = χ̄ odd: irreducible over F_p implies absolutely irreducible (R01.4).

nodes.title: A newform attached to E
nodes.statement: A normalised newform F of weight 2, of any level M ≥ 1, is attached to E when its character is trivial and A_ℓ(F) = a_ℓ(E) for all but finitely many primes ℓ. Here a_ℓ(E) is the ℓ-th coefficient of Mathlib's L-function of E, equal to ℓ + 1 − #Ẽ(F_ℓ) at a prime of good reduction. Two newforms attached to E have the same level and are equal. hypotheses: The condition concerns almost all primes, so it does not depend on the Weierstrass model of E and is unchanged under ℚ-isogeny.

Uniqueness is imported from Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 5, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-5-strong-multiplicity-one-and-the-eigenform-characterization. Its cross-level theorem takes two newforms of the same weight, of any levels M and M′, whose coefficients agree at almost all primes not dividing MM′, and concludes equality of levels, characters and forms. The pinned fixed-level theorem alone assumes agreement at all good indices outside a finite set and does not provide this statement.

Uniqueness: let F and G be attached to E, of levels M and M′. Their coefficients agree at all but finitely many primes, in particular at all but finitely many primes not dividing MM′. Layer 5's cross-level newform–newform theorem gives M = M′ and F = G. No local proof of strong multiplicity one is planned here.

nodes.title: A single newform with the Frobenius traces of E
nodes.statement: There is a normalised newform F of weight 2, trivial character and level N such that A_ℓ(F) = a_ℓ(E) for every prime ℓ ∤ N. In particular a newform attached to E exists.
hypotheses: The witnesses g_p of R29.2 are newforms of level exactly N, and the set of normalised newforms of weight 2, trivial character and level N is finite (Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 4).

Serre's own argument starts from an eigenform modulo p of level N and lifts its eigenvalues by Deligne–Serre; it yields a form of level dividing N, and Serre gets primitivity at level N from Carayol (Remarque 2). Here the classical Serre theorem supplies each witness as a newform of level N(ρ̄_{E,p}) = N, so F has level N at once. R29.4/exact-conductor proves, without the classical Serre theorem, that every newform attached to E has level N.
proofSteps: For p ∉ Σ_E take the witness g_p, a newform of weight 2, level N and trivial character (R29.2). Where the eigenvalue system is first obtained modulo p, as in Serre's text, Deligne–Serre lifting gives it in characteristic zero (R15.5); the witness of R29.2 is already in characteristic zero.
Pigeonhole: some F in the finite set of such newforms equals g_p for p in an infinite set P.
For ℓ ∤ N and p ∈ P ∖ {ℓ}: A_ℓ(F) − a_ℓ(E) ∈ λ_p, so A_ℓ(F) = a_ℓ(E) by algebraic-integer-norm-vanishing.
Only finitely many primes divide N, so F is attached to E.
acceptance: Only the good coefficients are compared here; the bad coefficients are R29.4.

nodes.title: A newform attached to E has rational integer coefficients
nodes.statement: Let F be a newform attached to E (attached-newform), of level M. Then the coefficient field of F is ℚ, and all its Fourier coefficients (including A_ℓ for ℓ | M) are rational integers. In particular this holds for F_E.
hypotheses: Trivial character; Galois conjugates of newforms are newforms of the same level and character (Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8g).
Only the property 'attached to E' is used, not the construction of F_E.
proofSteps: For σ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ), F^σ is a newform of level M and trivial character with A_ℓ(F^σ) = σ(A_ℓ(F)) = σ(a_ℓ(E)) = a_ℓ(E) for all but finitely many primes ℓ: F^σ is attached to E.

ModularForms Layer 5's prime-agreement strong multiplicity one gives F^σ = F; every coefficient is σ-fixed, hence rational. Coefficients of newforms are algebraic integers, so they lie in ℤ. The supplier is used at the single level M, with agreement only at almost all primes.

nodes.title: The Tate module of E is the Galois representation of a newform attached to E
nodes.statement: Let F be a newform attached to E. For every prime r, V_r(E) ≅ V_r(F) as ℚ_r[G_ℚ]-modules, where V_r(F) is the r-adic representation attached to F (Eichler–Shimura, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations). In particular V_r(E) ≅ V_r(F_E).
hypotheses: V_r(E) is semisimple (Faltings, R28.6). V_r(F) is semisimple because F has rational coefficients (rational-coefficient-field): its modular quotient is then an abelian variety of dimension 1 (ModularCurvesPartII R14.5/modular-quotient-dimension) whose rational Tate module is V_r(F) (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.6/weight-two-tate-module-decomposition), semisimple by Faltings again (R28.4, Satz 3). Irreducibility of V_r(F) is Ribet's theorem (cited as unpublished in Carayol 1986, 0.7 Remarque) and is not needed.
proofSteps: For all but finitely many primes ℓ, both representations are unramified at ℓ with characteristic polynomial X² − a_ℓ(E)X + ℓ for the arithmetic Frobenius (R01.6 for E; R19.1/newform-rank-two-realisation for F, whose coefficient A_ℓ(F) is a_ℓ(E) for almost all ℓ).

Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt (R01.5), which need the Frobenius polynomials only on a set of primes of density one, identify the semisimplifications; both representations are semisimple (hypothesis), hence isomorphic.
acceptance: Characteristic polynomials, not traces alone, when comparing residually.

nodes.title: All local factors agree
nodes.statement: Let F be a newform attached to E. For every prime ℓ, the local factor of E (Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial: 1 − a_ℓT + ℓT² at good ℓ, 1 ∓ T at split/nonsplit multiplicative ℓ, 1 at additive ℓ) equals the local factor 1 − A_ℓ(F)T + 𝟙_{ℓ∤N} ℓT² of F. Equivalently A_ℓ(F) = a_ℓ(E) at every ℓ ∤ N, and A_ℓ(F) = +1, −1, 0 according as E has split multiplicative, nonsplit multiplicative or additive reduction at ℓ | N. Hence A_n(F) is the n-th coefficient of Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.LFunction of E for every n ≥ 1. In particular this holds for F_E.
hypotheses: Uses the Weil–Deligne comparison at ℓ | N, not only traces.

Convention: V_r is the Tate module and Frobenius is arithmetic, so an Euler factor is read on the inertia coinvariants of V_r, equivalently with the geometric Frobenius on the inertia invariants of the dual.
proofSteps: F has level N (exact-conductor). For ℓ ∤ N and r ≠ ℓ both V_r(E) and V_r(F) are unramified at ℓ, with Frobenius polynomials X² − a_ℓ(E)X + ℓ and X² − A_ℓ(F)X + ℓ; they are isomorphic (tate-module-comparison), so A_ℓ(F) = a_ℓ(E) at every good prime, not only at almost all.

For ℓ | N and r ≠ ℓ the local factor of E is det(1 − Frob_ℓ T | V_r(E)_{I_ℓ}), the arithmetic Frobenius on the inertia coinvariants; equivalently det(1 − Frob_ℓ⁻¹ T | (V_r(E)^∨)^{I_ℓ}). (On the invariants V_r(E)^{I_ℓ} the arithmetic Frobenius acts by ℓ at a split multiplicative prime, which would give 1 − ℓT.) It is 1 ∓ T at a split or nonsplit multiplicative prime, by the Tate curve, and 1 at an additive prime, where the coinvariants vanish. For F the same determinant on V_r(F) is 1 − A_ℓ(F)T (R19.4/conductor-and-local-factors-classical, part (c)). The isomorphism V_r(E) ≅ V_r(F) identifies them.
The coefficients at prime powers and at composite indices follow from the Euler product on both sides.
acceptance: Check the sign convention against Mathlib's localPolynomial (split multiplicative gives 1 − T).

V_r(A_F) ≅ V_r(E) by tate-module-comparison; Faltings' isogeny criterion gives a ℚ-isogeny A_F → E.

nodes.title: The modular parametrisation X₀(N) → E
nodes.statement: Fix a ℚ-isogeny λ : A_{F_E} → E (isogeny-to-E). φ_E : X₀(N) → E is the composite of the Abel–Jacobi map X₀(N) → J₀(N) normalised at the rational cusp ∞, the quotient J₀(N) → A_{F_E} and λ. It is a nonconstant morphism of curves over ℚ with φ_E(∞) = O, and φ_E^*ω_E = c · 2πi F_E(z)dz for a constant c ∈ ℚ^×. φ_E depends on λ; for the optimal curve (E = A_{F_E}, λ = id) and ω_E a Néron differential, c is Manin's constant.
hypotheses: The Abel–Jacobi morphism at the rational cusp ∞ and its universal property: ModularCurvesPartII R14.6/rational-cusp-abel-jacobi, which instantiates Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer F.

The statements of R14.5 about differentials and about the Abel–Jacobi composite are made for the quotient of J₁(N); they pass to the quotient A_{F_E} of J₀(N) through the isogeny of R14.5/trivial-character-J0.
proofSteps: The Abel–Jacobi image of X₀(N) generates J₀(N), and J₀(N) → A_{F_E} → E is surjective, so φ_E is nonconstant.
The pullback of the invariant differential lies in the F_E-eigenspace of holomorphic differentials.
acceptance: The map is a morphism over ℚ, not a divisor class; its degree is positive.
Over ℂ, φ_E is z ↦ 2πi∫_{i∞}^z F_E(w)dw mod Λ, followed by the isogeny (Cremona §2.15.1).
φ_E depends on the chosen isogeny λ; statements about deg φ_E fix λ (e.g. of minimal degree).

nodes.title: V_r(E) is absolutely irreducible
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve and r a prime. Then V_r(E) is an absolutely irreducible representation of G_ℚ: the ℚ_r-span of the image of G_ℚ in End_{ℚ_r}(V_r(E)) is all of End_{ℚ_r}(V_r(E)), and V_r(E) ⊗_{ℚ_r} L is an irreducible L[G_ℚ]-module for every field extension L of ℚ_r. Curves with complex multiplication over ℚ̄ are included: their extra endomorphisms are not defined over ℚ.
hypotheses: The base field is ℚ. Over a number field containing the CM field of a CM curve, V_r(E) ⊗ ℚ̄_r is a sum of two characters and the statement fails.
End_ℚ(E) = ℤ for every E/ℚ, which RS-06 assigns to FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.6.
proofSteps: The commutant of G_ℚ in End_{ℚ_r}(V_r(E)) is End_ℚ(E) ⊗ ℚ_r, by the Tate–Hom comparison with E′ = E (R28.6/tate-hom-comparison-for-elliptic-curves). Since End_ℚ(E) = ℤ (R28.6), it is ℚ_r.

V_r(E) is semisimple (R28.6/semisimplicity-of-the-rational-tate-module-of-an-elliptic-curve). A semisimple module whose endomorphism ring is a field is simple: a nontrivial decomposition would give a nontrivial idempotent endomorphism.

Let A ⊆ End_{ℚ_r}(V_r(E)) be the ℚ_r-span of the image of G_ℚ, a subalgebra. It acts faithfully on the simple module V_r(E), so its radical is zero and A ≅ M_n(D) with V_r(E) ≅ Dⁿ and End_A(V_r(E)) ≅ D^op (Wedderburn). The commutant being ℚ_r gives D = ℚ_r and n = 2: A = End_{ℚ_r}(V_r(E)).
For a field L ⊇ ℚ_r, the L-span of the image of G_ℚ in End_L(V_r(E) ⊗ L) is A ⊗ L = End_L(V_r(E) ⊗ L), which leaves no proper nonzero subspace invariant.
acceptance: Test: for E: y² = x³ − x (CM by ℤ[i]) and r = 5, the restriction of V₅(E) to G_{ℚ(i)} is a sum of two characters, while V₅(E) ⊗ ℚ̄₅ is irreducible for G_ℚ: complex conjugation exchanges the two lines.
Semisimplicity alone does not give the statement: a sum of two characters is semisimple.

nodes.title: A quotient of J₀(N′) has an attached newform
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve of conductor N and let N′ ≥ 1. Suppose there is a surjective homomorphism π : J₀(N′) → E over ℚ. Then there are a divisor M of N′ and a normalised newform f of weight 2, level M and trivial character with A_ℓ(f) = a_ℓ(E) for all but finitely many primes ℓ: f is attached to E (attached-newform). Consequently f has rational integer coefficients, its level is N, N divides N′, and A_p(f) = a_p(E) at every prime p (rational-coefficient-field, exact-conductor, bad-euler-factors). The construction of f does not use the classical Serre theorem.
hypotheses: N′ is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the conductor of E.

A_f denotes the quotient of J₀(M) attached to a newform f of level M and trivial character (ModularCurvesPartII R14.5/trivial-character-J0, which writes it A_f⁰), and A_f¹ the quotient of J₁(M) (R14.5/modular-quotient). They are isogenous over ℚ, compatibly with the actions of K_f.

The old/new decomposition of the Jacobian over ℚ (requested from ModularCurvesPartII R14.5): J₀(N′) is ℚ-isogenous to ∏_{M ∣ N′} ∏_{[f]} (A_f)^{σ₀(N′/M)}, where the inner product runs over the Galois orbits [f] of normalised newforms of weight 2, level M and trivial character, and σ₀ counts positive divisors. R14.5/oldform-comparison states the analogue for one orbit in J₁; the request asks for the J₀ form and that the orbit parts exhaust J₀(N′).
proofSteps: Fix a prime r. The map V_r(π) : V_r(J₀(N′)) → V_r(E) is G_ℚ-equivariant and surjective (ModularCurvesPartII:R14.5/quotient-tate-exact).

Isogenies induce isomorphisms of rational Tate modules, so the decomposition gives V_r(J₀(N′)) ≅ ⊕_{M ∣ N′} ⊕_{[f]} V_r(A_f)^{σ₀(N′/M)}. A nonzero map out of a direct sum is nonzero on a summand: there are M ∣ N′, a newform f of level M and trivial character, and a nonzero G_ℚ-map u : V_r(A_f) → V_r(E).

V_r(A_f) ≅ V_r(A_f¹) as modules over K_f ⊗ ℚ_r with G_ℚ-action, by the isogeny of R14.5/trivial-character-J0. V_r(A_f¹) is free of rank 2 over K_f ⊗ ℚ_r and is the sum of the λ-adic representations of f (R19.6/weight-two-tate-module-decomposition), whose arithmetic Frobenius at ℓ ∤ Mr has characteristic polynomial X² − A_ℓ(f)X + ℓ (R19.1/newform-rank-two-realisation).

Extend scalars to an algebraic closure ℚ̄_r of ℚ_r. Since K_f ⊗ ℚ̄_r = ∏_σ ℚ̄_r over the embeddings σ : K_f → ℚ̄_r, V_r(A_f) ⊗ ℚ̄_r = ⊕_σ V_{f,σ}, where V_{f,σ} is two-dimensional, G_ℚ-stable and unramified at ℓ ∤ Mr with Frobenius characteristic polynomial X² − σ(A_ℓ(f))X + ℓ.

u ⊗ ℚ̄_r is nonzero, so its restriction to some V_{f,σ} is nonzero. Its target V_r(E) ⊗ ℚ̄_r is irreducible of dimension 2 (absolute-irreducibility-of-the-rational-tate-module), so the restriction is surjective, hence an isomorphism V_{f,σ} ≅ V_r(E) ⊗ ℚ̄_r of G_ℚ-representations.
Take traces of Frobenius at the primes ℓ ∤ NN′r: σ(A_ℓ(f)) = a_ℓ(E) (R01.6 for E). An isomorphism is at hand, so no density or Brauer–Nesbitt argument is needed.

Descend the embedding. Let ℚ̄ ⊂ ℂ be the algebraic closure of ℚ and fix an embedding ι : ℚ̄ → ℚ̄_r. The coefficient field K_f ⊂ ℚ̄ is a number field, so σ = ι ∘ τ for a unique embedding τ : K_f → ℚ̄. As ι is injective and fixes ℤ, τ(A_ℓ(f)) = a_ℓ(E) for every prime ℓ ∤ NN′r.

The conjugate f^τ = Σ τ(A_n(f))qⁿ is a normalised newform of weight 2, level M and trivial character (Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8g) with A_ℓ(f^τ) = a_ℓ(E) for every prime ℓ ∤ NN′r. It is attached to E; rename it f.
Apply rational-coefficient-field, exact-conductor and bad-euler-factors to f: integer coefficients, level M = N, hence N ∣ N′, and A_p(f) = a_p(E) at every prime p.
acceptance: Level test: N′ = 22 and E = 11a1 = J₀(11), with π either degeneracy map J₀(22) → J₀(11). S₂(Γ₀(22)) has no new part and V_r(J₀(22)) ≅ V_r(A_f)² for the level-11 form f; the theorem returns f, of level 11, a proper divisor of 22.

Coefficient-field test: N′ = 23. S₂(Γ₀(23)) is one Galois orbit with K_f = ℚ(√5) and A₂(f) = (−1 ± √5)/2, and J₀(23) = A_f has dimension 2. No embedding σ makes all σ(A_ℓ(f)) rational, so no elliptic curve over ℚ is a quotient of J₀(23).

Semisimplicity of V_r(E) alone does not identify it with one V_{f,σ}: irreducibility is what turns the nonzero map into an isomorphism. Irreducibility of V_{f,σ} (Ribet, part of R19.1/newform-rank-two-realisation) would serve as well; the proof uses the E-side statement.

Non-circularity: neither this node nor any node it depends on in this packet (attached-newform, rational-coefficient-field, tate-module-comparison, exact-conductor, bad-euler-factors, absolute-irreducibility-of-the-rational-tate-module) has the Serre witnesses, a-single-newform-for-infinitely-many-p-and-exact-coefficients or newform-of-E among its prerequisites.

nodes.title: Modularity of elliptic curves over ℚ
nodes.statement: Every elliptic curve E/ℚ of conductor N is modular, in each of three equivalent formulations: (i) there is a normalised newform F of weight 2, level N and trivial character with rational integer coefficients and A_p(F) = a_p(E) for all primes p (with the bad-prime convention of bad-euler-factors); (ii) there is a surjective homomorphism J₀(N) → E over ℚ, so E is ℚ-isogenous to a quotient of J₀(N) and is itself one, as Serre notes; (iii) there is a nonconstant morphism X₀(N) → E over ℚ sending ∞ to O. All three hold unconditionally, through the classical Serre theorem (ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6). Their equivalence does not use that theorem: for an elliptic curve E/ℚ, the existence of a newform attached to E, of a surjective homomorphism J₀(N′) → E over ℚ for some N′ ≥ 1, and of a nonconstant morphism X₀(N′) → E over ℚ for some N′ ≥ 1 are equivalent; the newform then has level N, the level N′ is a multiple of N, and N′ = N is possible.
hypotheses: Scope: elliptic curves over ℚ only.
In (ii) and (iii) the level N′ of a quotient or parametrisation need not be the conductor; the equivalence shows that N ∣ N′.
proofSteps: The three statements hold: a-single-newform-for-infinitely-many-p-and-exact-coefficients gives the newform F_E attached to E (newform-of-E), of level N. (i) is rational-coefficient-field and bad-euler-factors for F_E; (ii) is isogeny-to-E composed with the quotient J₀(N) → A_{F_E}; (iii) is modular-parametrisation.

Attached newform ⇒ quotient and parametrisation at level N, without R27.6: let F be a newform attached to E. It has level N (exact-conductor), and isogeny-to-E gives a ℚ-isogeny A_F → E from the quotient A_F of J₀(N). Composing with the quotient map gives a surjective homomorphism J₀(N) → E over ℚ; composing further with the Abel–Jacobi morphism at ∞ gives a morphism X₀(N) → E over ℚ that sends ∞ to O and is nonconstant (ModularCurvesPartII R14.6/rational-cusp-abel-jacobi, R14.5/abel-jacobi-composite-nonzero).

Parametrisation ⇒ quotient: let φ : X₀(N′) → E be nonconstant over ℚ. After translation by −φ(∞) ∈ E(ℚ) it sends ∞ to O. By the universal property of the Abel–Jacobi morphism at ∞ (R14.6/rational-cusp-abel-jacobi, Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer F) it factors through a homomorphism J₀(N′) → E over ℚ, which is surjective because its image is an abelian subvariety containing φ(X₀(N′)) = E.
Quotient ⇒ attached newform: newform-from-a-modular-quotient. By the second step the newform has level N, so N ∣ N′.
acceptance: Dependency check: the chain R29.1–R29.5 uses R27.6 but no statement that assumes E modular.

Oldform regression: N = 22 has dim J₀(22) = 2 and dim V_r(J₀(22)) = 4. The single level-11 rational newform occurs twice, through f(z) and f(2z); a sum with one copy per primitive newform incorrectly has dimension 2.
Level regression: 11a1 is a quotient of J₀(22), and the newform this gives is the level-11 form; a quotient of J₀(N′) only shows N ∣ N′.
The equivalence of the three formulations is proved without R27.6; only the first proof step, their truth, uses it.

In general the character is conjugated as well; preservation of the character here uses that it is trivial.

The old/new decomposition of the Jacobian J₀(N′) over ℚ: J₀(N′) is ℚ-isogenous to ∏_{M ∣ N′} ∏_{[f]} (A_f)^{σ₀(N′/M)}, where the inner product runs over the Galois orbits of normalised newforms of weight 2, level M and trivial character, A_f is the quotient of J₀(M) attached to f (the A_f⁰ of the node trivial-character-J0), and σ₀ is the number of positive divisors. The node oldform-comparison states the part attached to one orbit for J₁; needed are its J₀ form and that the orbit parts exhaust J₀(N′) up to isogeny, from ModularForms Layer 4's decomposition of S₂(Γ₀(N′)) into old and new classes. R19.6's comparison for an individual quotient does not imply it. The Abel–Jacobi morphism of a curve with a rational point and its universal property.
Analytic continuation and functional equation of L(f, s) for a weight-two newform with trivial character.

Cross-level strong multiplicity one in weight two (Miyake 4.6.19): if normalised newforms f, g of weight 2 and trivial character, of nonzero levels M, M′, have A_ℓ(f) = A_ℓ(g) for all but finitely many primes ℓ ∤ MM′, then M = M′ and the forms agree after transport to that level. Both inputs must be newforms; no same-level conclusion is available for a level-raised old eigenform. Import the Layer 5 theorem, not a new proof in R29.3. It is used for two newforms attached to E (attached-newform), and at a single level for a newform and its Galois conjugates (rational-coefficient-field).
